about.description:
zsasa calculates the solvent accessible surface area of proteins and other
molecules with the Shrake-Rupley and Lee-Richards algorithms. It reads
mmCIF, BinaryCIF, PDB, SDF/MOL and JSON structures, processes whole
directories of them, and analyses XTC, TRR, DCD and AMBER NetCDF
trajectories. It is multi-threaded and SIMD-accelerated.

`zsasa` is the Python package (NumPy API, integrations with Gemmi,
Biopython, Biotite, MDTraj and MDAnalysis) and brings the command line
program with it. `zsasa-cli` is the command line program alone, and
`libzsasa` the shared library with the C ABI.
about.summary: Shared library of the zsasa solvent accessible surface area calculator (C ABI)

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.10.1"
  # Zig packages zsasa is built from, as resolved from build.zig.zon:
  #   zsasa -> ztraj -> zsasa 0.2.11 (an older release, for ztraj's own SASA code) -> zxdrfile
  # When updating, follow the `.dependencies` of each build.zig.zon and keep
  # these three in step. A stale entry cannot go unnoticed: build.sh/build.bat
  # let Zig recompute each package hash, and `zig build --system` only accepts
  # the hashes that build.zig.zon asks for.
  ztraj_version: "0.8.0"
  zsasa_dep_version: "0.2.11"
  zxdrfile_version: "0.4.0"
  # Zig compiles for the build machine (its CPU and OS version) unless it is
  # given a target, and it does not read MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET. Spell the
  # target out from the conda-forge pinning instead: c_stdlib_version is the
  # glibc version on linux and the deployment target on osx. This is also what
  # makes cross-compiled builds (osx-arm64 from osx-64, linux-aarch64 from
  # linux-64) correct: Zig is a cross-compiler for every target out of the box.
  zig_target: >-
    ${{
      "x86_64-linux-gnu."  ~ c_stdlib_version if host_platform == "linux-64"      else
      "aarch64-linux-gnu." ~ c_stdlib_version if host_platform == "linux-aarch64" else
      "x86_64-macos."      ~ c_stdlib_version if host_platform == "osx-64"        else
      "aarch64-macos."     ~ c_stdlib_version if host_platform == "osx-arm64"     else
      "x86_64-windows-gnu"                    if host_platform == "win-64"        else
      ""
    }}

recipe:
  name: zsasa-split
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://github.com/N283T/zsasa/archive/refs/tags/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 219151e12b22c5f5c848fa8889ed4baed97d076e2becc893894ab56a78d8987d
  # Zig package dependencies. `zig build` would download these; the build has
  # no network access, so they are listed here and handed to Zig as local
  # directories (see build.sh).
  - url: https://github.com/N283T/ztraj/archive/refs/tags/v${{ ztraj_version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: c7abf6d94b9ca401e07752fe2f99502c50f79321d2f9558969464151cba2628a
    target_directory: zig-deps/ztraj
  - url: https://github.com/N283T/zsasa/archive/refs/tags/v${{ zsasa_dep_version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: 72f7e50e3eb00341a7f10ca144134a09b0cad5b8c414156cc98beb625ee05bb9
    target_directory: zig-deps/zsasa
  - url: https://github.com/N283T/zxdrfile/archive/refs/tags/v${{ zxdrfile_version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: daffd0008cdac67b3485f12c169a93b6f6e7f0287a1a85caf0b2ba706606f644
    target_directory: zig-deps/zxdrfile

build:
  number: 1

outputs:
  # Build once: the program and the library come out of the same `zig build`.
  - staging:
      name: zsasa-build
    requirements:
      build:
        - zig >=0.16.0,<0.17
        # Zig brings its own libc stubs and needs no C compiler or sysroot. The
        # stdlib package is listed for its run-export, which libzsasa and
        # zsasa-cli inherit: it puts the __glibc / __osx lower bound on them, the
        # same c_stdlib_version zig_target uses.
        - if: unix
          then: ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    build:
      script:
        file: build
        env:
          ZIG_TARGET: ${{ zig_target }}

  # The shared library with the C ABI. It is what the Python package loads.
  - package:
      name: libzsasa
    inherit: zsasa-build
    build:
      dynamic_linking:
        # libzsasa links against the system C library only, so there is no RPATH
        # to rewrite. Zig also leaves no header padding in Mach-O files, so
        # install_name_tool cannot add one ("larger updated load commands do
        # not fit").
        binary_relocation: false
        # Without an LC_RPATH the library's own install name
        # (@rpath/libzsasa.dylib) is not recognised as the library itself and
        # is reported as overlinking.
        missing_dso_allowlist:
          - if: osx
            then: "@rpath/libzsasa.dylib"
      # The staging build installs the program and the library; keep the library.
      files:
        include:
          - if: unix
            then: lib/libzsasa.*
            else:
              - Library/bin/zsasa.dll
              - Library/lib/zsasa.lib
    requirements:
      run:
        # On Windows Zig links against its bundled mingw-w64, which uses the
        # Universal CRT (api-ms-win-crt-*.dll) and nothing from the MSVC
        # runtime that stdlib('c') would add.
        - if: win
          then: ucrt
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          lib:
            - zsasa
      # The library has no command line: load it and call the C API.
      - script:
          - python test_libzsasa.py ${{ version }}
        requirements:
          run:
            - python
        files:
          recipe:
            - test_libzsasa.py
    about:
      summary: Shared library of the zsasa solvent accessible surface area calculator (C ABI)

  # The command line program: a self-contained executable that does not use
  # libzsasa (on linux it is fully static).
  - package:
      name: zsasa-cli
    inherit: zsasa-build
    build:
      dynamic_linking:
        binary_relocation: false
      # The staging build installs the program and the library; keep the program.
      files:
        include:
          - if: unix
            then: bin/zsasa
            else: Library/bin/zsasa.exe
    requirements:
      run:
        - if: win
          then: ucrt
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          bin:
            - zsasa
      - script:
          - if: unix
            then:
              - zsasa --version | grep -Fx "zsasa ${{ version }}"
              - zsasa calc examples/1ubq.pdb sasa.json
              # 4834.72 A^2 is the value upstream documents for 1ubq.
              - grep -E "total_area.+4834[.]7" sasa.json
            else:
              - zsasa --version | findstr /C:"zsasa ${{ version }}"
              - zsasa calc examples/1ubq.pdb sasa.json
              - findstr /R /C:"total_area.*4834[.]7" sasa.json
        files:
          source:
            - examples/1ubq.pdb
    about:
      summary: Command line program of the zsasa solvent accessible surface area calculator

  # The Python package, with what `pip install zsasa` provides: the Python API
  # and the zsasa command. The wheel on PyPI bundles the library and the
  # program; here they are the two packages above.
  - package:
      name: zsasa
    build:
      noarch: python
      # One package serves every platform and Python version: build it once, in
      # the linux-64 job, next to the libzsasa and zsasa-cli it is tested with.
      skip: not (linux and x86_64)
      script:
        env:
          # python/hatch_build.py: build a pure-Python wheel, compile and
          # bundle nothing. The package then loads libzsasa from the
          # environment.
          ZSASA_NO_BUNDLE: "1"
        content:
          - python -m pip install ./python -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
          # pyproject.toml declares a `zsasa` console script that runs the
          # program bundled in a wheel. In this package `zsasa` is the program
          # of zsasa-cli itself, at the very path pip writes the script to, so
          # the script must not be packaged (and python.entry_points is left
          # out for the same reason).
          - rm "${PREFIX}/bin/zsasa"
    requirements:
      host:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        - pip
        - hatchling
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - numpy >=1.24
        - cffi >=1.15
        # The Python package checks the ABI version of the library and calls
        # its functions by name, so it goes with the library of its own release.
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("libzsasa", lower_bound="x.x.x", upper_bound="x.x.x") }}
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("zsasa-cli", lower_bound="x.x.x", upper_bound="x.x.x") }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - zsasa
          pip_check: true
          python_version:
            - ${{ python_min }}.*
            - "*"
      - script:
          - python test_python.py ${{ version }}
        requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
        files:
          recipe:
            - test_python.py
    about:
      summary: Fast solvent accessible surface area (SASA) calculator written in Zig, with Python bindings

about:
  homepage: https://n283t.github.io/zsasa/
  summary: Fast solvent accessible surface area (SASA) calculator written in Zig
  description: |
    zsasa calculates the solvent accessible surface area of proteins and other
    molecules with the Shrake-Rupley and Lee-Richards algorithms. It reads
    mmCIF, BinaryCIF, PDB, SDF/MOL and JSON structures, processes whole
    directories of them, and analyses XTC, TRR, DCD and AMBER NetCDF
    trajectories. It is multi-threaded and SIMD-accelerated.

    `zsasa` is the Python package (NumPy API, integrations with Gemmi,
    Biopython, Biotite, MDTraj and MDAnalysis) and brings the command line
    program with it. `zsasa-cli` is the command line program alone, and
    `libzsasa` the shared library with the C ABI.
  # zsasa and ztraj are MIT; the XTC/TRR reader in ztraj and zxdrfile derives
  # from libxdrfile (BSD-2-Clause). All of them are compiled into the binaries.
  license: MIT AND BSD-2-Clause
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
    - zig-deps/ztraj/LICENSE
    - zig-deps/ztraj/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
    - zig-deps/zsasa/LICENSE
    - zig-deps/zxdrfile/LICENSE
  documentation: https://n283t.github.io/zsasa/
  repository: https://github.com/N283T/zsasa

extra:
  feedstock-name: zsasa
  recipe-maintainers:
    - N283T
